encounter.notes: Large winged draconic construct. NOT humanoid: wingspan fills the frame, body core is narrow, skull sits mid-height below the wing shoulders, long tail.

reference.pose_mismatch: UNRESOLVED and known. The front plate shows the tail short and tucked between the legs; the back shows it long and swept down-left, and the wing sweep differs too. Two-view reconstruction and the per-slice silhouette registration both assume a single pose. Consequence: expect a smeared tail and wing-sweep error. Built anyway with the defect documented rather than fabricating a matched plate.

geometry.provenance: Tencent Hunyuan3D-2mv (fp16, 50 steps, octree 380, seed 12345) from letterboxed view-01/view-03 (2415px square, full 1801/1856px wingspan retained). Draft: 194,988 faces, single watertight shell, 91.3s. HERO TRIANGLE BUDGET 70,000 (approved exception above the 20-50k standard): two ~1.8 unit membranes plus a long tail leave very few triangles per unit area at 45k, and thin sheets are the weakest case for marching-cubes reconstruction.
geometry.budget_note: 70,000 chosen inside the approved 70-80k hero band. 75,000 built to 2,447,876 bytes, only 52KB under the 2.5MB gate; 70,000 leaves usable headroom at no visible cost.

uv_density.note: Legacy scalar warp disabled; regions.boxes drives the density warp instead.

rights: The Elder Scrolls Online name, character design and related rights remain with ZeniMax Media/Bethesda Softworks. Reconstructed from published screenshots for an authorized fan prototype; not a claim that the IP is freely licensed.

regions.note: No scalar head_v_min: this NPC's skull sits MID-HEIGHT below the wing shoulders, so the top of the silhouette is wing, not head, and no height threshold can select it. Boxes verified visually on a membership render (build/saint-olms/box-check/sheet.png): red claims only the horned skull, blue/green only the two membrane wings, body/legs/tail unclaimed.
regions.targeting_rationale: Both the skull and the wing membranes are boosted, and tuned to land at roughly 200^2 front-facing EACH (skull 202^2, wings 203^2/213^2) rather than chasing the humanoid 'face >=256^2'. There is no single face region on a winged construct: identity is split between a small skull that anchors it at closeup and two large membranes that dominate the silhouette at replay distance. Equal texel squares give the skull far higher density per unit area (~2% of surface vs the wings' ~45%), which is the correct bias. Boxes compete directly - measured: skull 3.0/wing 2.0 gave skull 148^2, skull 4.5/wing 2.0 gave wings 183^2 - so pushing either to 256^2 starves the other.
